c74object.name: bachmcp.onnx~
c74object.digest: Hear a signal live with a sound model
c74object.description: Runs a sound model of models/audio/ on a signal, live: a tagger (CED) names what it hears with AudioSet labels and scores, a CLAP (LAION CLAP, CLAP2) compares the sound with texts or gives its embedding. The same models the bach-mcp server uses, as ONNX: download them with python py/main.py download <name>. The audio thread only keeps the last 32 seconds of the signal; every hop seconds, while DSP runs, the last window seconds are resampled to the model's rate and heard on a worker thread. The answer comes as dictionary <name> out of the left outlet, then a bang out of the right one. If the model is still busy at the next hop, that hop is skipped: answers come as fast as the model can give them and never pile up. Objects loading the same model share it. Apple Silicon only; ONNX Runtime comes with python py/main.py install (into support/), and this object loads its core from bachmcp.onnxb~, which must sit next to it.

outlet.digest: dictionary: the answer (tags / similarity / embedding), every hop seconds
bang after each answer; model <name> <kind> <sr> <window>; error

method.name: signal
method.description: One channel: mix several before the inlet. Heard at Max's sample rate and resampled to the model's.

attribute.name: model
attribute.description: A sound model name of models/catalog.toml (in models/audio/), or a model folder's full path. Taggers: ced-base, ced-mini (16 kHz, 10 s). LAION CLAP: laion-clap-music-speech, laion-clap-general, laion-clap-small (48 kHz, 10 s). CLAP2: laion-clap2-m, laion-clap2-l (32 kHz, 30 s). It loads on a worker thread; when it is ready the right outlet says model <name> <kind> <samplerate> <window>. Live, a small model answers faster: ced-mini, laion-clap-small, laion-clap2-m.

attribute.name: window
attribute.description: Each answer hears the last this many seconds. 0 (default): the model's own, at most 10 s. Up to 31 s. A LAION CLAP hears 10 s at most: a longer window is cut, with a warning. Right after DSP starts, the window holds only what was heard so far.

attribute.name: hop
attribute.description: How often the last window seconds are sent to the model (0.05 at least). A hop that comes while the model is still busy is skipped, so a slow model answers less often than this. With DSP off, or no new sound, nothing is sent.

attribute.name: active
attribute.description: 0: no answers (the signal is still kept, so turning it on again answers at the next hop with the last window seconds). 1 (default): answer every hop seconds.

attribute.name: samplerate
attribute.digest: Sample rate fed to the model (Hz)
attribute.description: 0 (default): the model's own rate (16000 CED, 48000 LAION CLAP, 32000 CLAP2); the signal is resampled to it from Max's rate. Any other rate is used as given, with a warning: the model was trained at its own rate and its answers may be wrong.

attribute.name: labels
attribute.description: A tagger's answer has at most this many labels, the highest scores first.

attribute.name: threshold
attribute.description: A tagger leaves out labels scoring below this (scores are 0-1). If none reaches it, tags is empty.

attribute.name: text
attribute.description: Each atom is one text (quote texts with spaces: "A drum loop plays." "A man is speaking."). They are embedded once, when set or when the model loads; each answer then says, in this order, the cosine between the sound and each text (about -1 to 1; higher is closer, and only the order between texts means much). LAION's CLAPs were trained on captions: full sentences work better than single words. A tagger ignores it, with a warning.

attribute.name: embedding
attribute.description: 1: a CLAP's answer also holds the sound's embedding, a unit vector (512 numbers for LAION CLAP, 640 CLAP2-M, 960 CLAP2-L), to compare sounds with each other. A CLAP with no text and embedding 0 has nothing to say, and warns so.

c74object.discussion: The answer is a dictionary the object owns, filled again at each answer: copy it (dict) to keep it past the next hop. Its keys: model and kind (tagger, clap, clap2); samplerate, the Hz the model was fed; duration, the ms heard; a tagger's tags, an array of { label, score }, highest first; a CLAP's similarity, an array of { text, score } in text order, and embedding with embedding 1.
